# Nehemiah 6: Research Notes

**Before you use these notes:**
- **Denominational differences (item 2):** I found none. The older commentators I read come from different traditions: Gill was a Baptist, Matthew Henry a Nonconformist (Presbyterian-type), Guzik writes from a Calvary Chapel / charismatic-leaning background, and Coffman was from the Churches of Christ. On this chapter they all read it the same basic way. The real disagreements are about wording and grammar, and they are marked **[debated]** below.
- **Gaps:** I didn't get to any Catholic or Orthodox commentary sites, bibleodyssey, or netbible's notes. I also found nothing on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter. The only Catholic material below comes from Catholic Bible translations.
- **v. 17 and v. 19:** These have less coverage. The Enduring Word page I read was cut off after v. 16.

---

**v. 1** – The gaps in the wall were closed but the gates weren't hung yet. Guzik calls this a "now-or-never" moment for the enemies: if they didn't act right away, the wall would be finished. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Getz says this time the enemies attacked Nehemiah himself. Removing him or ruining his credibility might stop the work. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary
- Utley notes that tradition makes Geshem king of Kedar in northwest Arabia, a powerful figure in the Persian empire. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 2** – The invitation looked friendly, perhaps an offer to make peace, but Nehemiah saw through it. Guzik's main theme is discernment. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Barnes: Ono was chosen to draw Nehemiah far away from his supporters so he could be attacked more easily. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-2.htm
- The Pulpit Commentary says "do me mischief" is a polite way of saying they planned to murder him. Keil & Delitzsch says they probably meant to take him prisoner, perhaps kill him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-2.htm
- **[debated] Where was Ono?** Estimates range from 12 to about 30 miles from Jerusalem. Constable puts it near Lod, in a kind of no-man's-land between Judah and Samaria, and says the trip would have taken Nehemiah away for at least two days. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/6-2.html Keil & Delitzsch prefers a site north-west of Jerusalem near Bethel. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-2.htm
- **[debated] "Villages" or a place name?** Some take the Hebrew word as the name of a village, "Kephirim" (Rashi, Pulpit). Keil & Delitzsch disagrees. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-2.htm Constable mentions a third option: "with the lions," a picture for the regional rulers. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/6-2.html
- Ellicott thinks Tobiah isn't named here because he would only attend as Sanballat's secretary. https://biblehub.com/nehemiah/6-2.htm

**v. 3** – Guzik: discernment kept Nehemiah focused, so he wasn't even distracted. Many good causes are not what we are called to do at the moment. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Steven Cole: this wasn't arrogance. Nehemiah knew his God-given task mattered, and walls without gates were as useless as no walls. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary
- Matthew Henry's application: answer invitations to idle gatherings with "we have work to do." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-2.htm

**v. 4** – Matthew Henry: when the same temptation comes again, resist it with the same reason and resolve. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/6-2.html
- Cole: the devil keeps repeating the same temptation to wear us down. He compares Delilah wearing Samson out. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 5** – Why "unsealed"?
- Barnes: so the contents would become widely known and frighten the Jews into stopping. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-9.htm
- Jamieson-Fausset-Brown: open letters were sent to inferiors, so this was a deliberate insult. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-9.htm
- Constable: the letter was really aimed at all the Jews, to make them doubt their leader's motives. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/6-9.html
- Layman's Bible Commentary offers another possibility: "open letter" may mean a message written on a piece of pottery. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lbc/nehemiah-6.html

**vv. 6–7** – Guzik: vague "everyone is saying" claims are a common way to start slander. A lie doesn't become true because it is popular. The charge stung because Nehemiah had made personal sacrifices precisely to stay blameless. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Matthew Henry: malicious people often present their own opinion as what everyone thinks. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_006.cfm
- Light of Israel: Artaxerxes had once before been persuaded that Jerusalem was a rebellious city (Ezra 4:19). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/loi/nehemiah-6.html
- Layman's: mentioning "prophets" shows Sanballat knew that prophets had often backed kings in Israel's history. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lbc/nehemiah-6.html

**v. 8** – Guzik: Nehemiah calmly called it a lie and kept working. He didn't argue point by point, because facts won't satisfy people like Sanballat. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Henry Morris: the right response was to deny the charges and keep going. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 9** – Matthew Henry: when enemies try to weaken our hands, we can go to God in prayer for strength. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_006.cfm
- Cambridge Bible: "made us afraid" really means "tried to." The text doesn't say they succeeded. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-9.htm
- **[debated] A prayer, or a resolve?** The words "O God" are not in the Hebrew.
  - Keil & Delitzsch and the Pulpit Commentary read the verb as a command addressed to God, so it is a prayer.
  - The Cambridge Bible leans toward "I will strengthen my hands."
  - The old Greek and Latin translations have "I strengthened my hands."
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-9.htm
  - Utley adds that the NJB, NAB, NEB and NET follow those old translations. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary
- **Catholic translations:** Douay-Rheims and the NAB both make it Nehemiah's resolve, e.g. NAB "I then redoubled my efforts." https://biblehub.com/nehemiah/6-9.htm

**v. 10** – Who was Shemaiah, and why was he "confined"?
- Jamieson-Fausset-Brown: a priest's son who claimed to be a prophet and had been secretly bribed. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-10.htm
- **[debated] Why he was "shut up":**
  - Ritual uncleanness (Pulpit, Gaebelein). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/nehemiah-6.html
  - Light of Israel rejects that, since he was planning to go into the temple, and thinks he was faking fear. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/loi/nehemiah-6.html
  - A put-on show of special devotion (Poole). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-10.htm
  - A symbolic acted-out prophecy. Keil & Delitzsch says either this or faked fear is possible. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-10.htm
- Pulpit: "within the temple" means the holy place, between the porch and the holy of holies. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-10.htm
- Constable mentions A. L. Ivry's suggestion that Shemaiah wanted them to take over the temple, but thinks it unlikely. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/dcc/nehemiah-6.html

**v. 11** – Two reasons for refusing. As governor he couldn't be seen to run, and entering priests-only space would break the Law (Cambridge). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-10.htm
- Guzik compares King Uzziah, who was struck with leprosy for entering the temple (2 Chr 26). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Precept Austin notes that ordinary people could take refuge at the altar in the courtyard, but not inside the temple building. Utley adds that Nehemiah may also have been a eunuch, which would also have barred him. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary
- Matthew Henry's application: "Should such a man as I…?" Christians should ask the same about their own conduct. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-10.htm

**v. 12** – Constable: the "prophecy" couldn't be from God because it told him to disobey the Law of Moses. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/6-10.html
- Preacher's Homiletical Commentary: test all advice ("prove all things"). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/phc/nehemiah-6.html

**v. 13** – Ryrie: if Nehemiah had gone in, his testimony would have been ruined. Henry Morris: he would rather die than commit sacrilege. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 14** – Guzik: instead of lashing out, Nehemiah handed his enemies over to God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- Noadiah is mentioned nowhere else (Believer's Study Bible). https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary
- Pulpit: Ewald's idea that she took a bribe is "wholly uncertain." https://studylight.org/commentaries/tpc/nehemiah-6.html
- Coffman sees the whole temple circle as hostile to Nehemiah. https://studylight.org/commentaries/bcc/nehemiah-6.html

**v. 15** – Why only 52 days? Benson and Poole give several reasons: the walls weren't fully torn down, the old stones were still there, there were many builders, the work was well organized, and God helped. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-15.htm
- Guzik: Nehemiah spent longer in prayer (four months) than the building took. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
- **[debated] Josephus** says the work took two years and four months. Gill, Barnes and Ellicott reject this. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-15.htm Lange thinks Josephus wanted to make the story less miraculous for his readers. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lcc/nehemiah-6.html
- **[debated] Counted from when?** Most count from the start of the work. Aben Ezra and the Geneva notes count from the reply to Sanballat. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-15.htm
- Ryrie dates the completion to Sept. 21, 444 B.C. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 16** – Ellicott: "done by our God" means with God's approval and help, not a miracle. Nehemiah gives God the glory and leaves out his own part. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-15.htm
- Lange: the enemies' problem was not lack of evidence but hearts turned away from God. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lcc/nehemiah-6.html
- Utley: "in their own eyes" is the Eastern idea of losing face. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 17** – Constable suggests this problem may have troubled Nehemiah throughout the whole building project. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/6-18.html
- Guzik pictures these Jewish nobles not seeing Tobiah's evil first-hand: "He's always been nice to us." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/

**v. 18** – Ellicott: these family ties led to a conspiracy, sealed by oath, against the governor. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/nehemiah-6.html
- Matthew Henry: "A sinful love leads to a sinful league." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-18.htm
- Poole links this to Ezra's breaking up of forbidden marriages. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-18.htm
- Keil & Delitzsch: Tobiah and his son have Jewish names, so they may have descended from northern Israelites. The high priest was also related to him (13:4). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-18.htm
- **[debated] What was the oath?** Cambridge reads it as an oath made when a family welcomed in a new in-law. It also allows a more general sense: nobles conspiring with him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/6-18.htm Cole and Precept Austin read "bound by oath" as business contracts. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**v. 19** – Utley: the nobles tried to make Tobiah look good, but his letters meant to frighten Nehemiah show what he was really like. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary
- Cole: the enemy lost the battle, so he turned to infiltration. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-6-commentary

**Christ-centred reading (vv. 1–14)** – Guzik draws a parallel. "Come down to Ono" echoes "come down from the cross." Jesus was also slandered and also offered an easier way out. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-6/
